subject.title: [Bug]: Native Talk button triggers OpenAI Realtime WebRTC call and fails with 500 when Realtime is not configured

question: Should Control UI browser Talk start from implicit OpenAI realtime credential availability, or only after an explicit Gateway realtime readiness/preflight says this session can start?
rationale: Current code and docs allow browser Talk through OpenAI realtime provider/auth resolution, while the report expects local/non-Realtime Talk setup not to start OpenAI Realtime; either answer changes visible setup semantics and possibly existing users.

options.title: Gate on Gateway realtime readiness
options.body: Use a Gateway-owned readiness/preflight result to disable or block Talk before microphone/WebRTC startup while preserving whichever credential policy maintainers choose.

options.title: Keep implicit credential activation
options.body: Accept that configured OpenAI realtime credentials enable browser Talk and limit the remaining fix to clearer provider/API error messaging.

options.title: Require explicit realtime config
options.body: Only show or start browser Talk when `talk.realtime` is explicitly configured, with an upgrade note or migration for users relying on implicit auth.

recommendation.title: Gate on Gateway realtime readiness
recommendation.body: Use a Gateway-owned readiness/preflight result to disable or block Talk before microphone/WebRTC startup while preserving whichever credential policy maintainers choose.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent merged OpenAI realtime auth and docs decision came through this owner trail, and the remaining question is policy for that same auth-enabled browser Talk surface.
